title: CognitiveArm: Enabling Real-Time EEG-Controlled Prosthetic Arm Using Embodied Machine Learning
problem: Real-time EEG processing for brain-controlled prosthetics requires efficient on-device inference (filtering, feature extraction, classification) while maintaining low latency and high accuracy on resource-constrained edge hardware.
motivation: Non-invasive brain-computer interfaces enable prosthetic control, but achieving real-time performance on edge devices is challenging due to model complexity and latency constraints.
method: The system reads brain signals using the BrainFlow library and trains deep learning models to interpret them for prosthetic control. It searches through different combinations of settings—such as network size, learning algorithms, data window sizes, and whether to combine multiple models—using evolutionary search (testing random variations and keeping what works best) to find configurations that maintain accuracy while running on resource-limited hardware. To make these models small enough for the prosthetic device, it removes unnecessary connections from the networks (pruning) and converts numbers to lower precision (quantization). Users can switch between different control modes with voice commands.
key_novelty: It searches for and compresses deep learning models that balance accuracy and speed for real-time prosthetic control on resource-limited hardware.
contributions: Real-time EEG processing on embedded hardware with <latency guarantee mentioned
90% accuracy in classifying three core actions (left, right, idle)
Pareto-optimal model search through evolutionary tuning
Model compression via pruning and quantization
Voice-command multiplexing for multi-action control (e.g., handshake, cup picking)
Full prototype with OpenBCI UltraCortex Mark IV integration
limitations: Evaluation on only three DoF prosthetic arm; generalization to more complex limbs unclear.
primary_theme: Real-time EEG-driven prosthetic control via optimized edge ML
